question: How confidently must the overseer believe an existing tile fits the situation before it runs the tile instead of escalating to the author
pole_low: escalates on any doubt, quality over cost, the library stays thin
pole_high: runs the closest tile almost always, cost over fit, the library stays small by force
why: This single threshold sets the whole system's economics: the LLM pulse rate, the budget burn, and how often play visibly stumbles. Stated by Casey 2026-10-14: the Jev must be able to say none of these are good enough
evidence_needed: Session logs once the tile runner exists: escalation rate vs session quality, plus Voyager's verification economics as the published baseline

question: When an interruption appears mid-plan, how much better than the A-plan must it score before the avatar bends toward it
pole_low: bends for any edge, lively but jittery, plans rarely complete
pole_high: bends only for a clear win, steady but misses quiet opportunities
why: Casey's trolling rule: you hope to be interrupted, but a text from a nearby boat does not make you beeline. The bend threshold is the avatar's opportunism dial and the coach will want to see it
evidence_needed: Session logs: interruptions offered vs taken vs regretted, coach overrides as the ground truth of a wrong threshold

question: When bending toward an interruption, how much should the route harvest value on the way (good water en route) versus arriving fast
pole_low: beeline, arrive fast, pass up everything between
pole_high: harvest route, slower arrival, value collected on the way compounds
why: Casey, 2026-10-14: you never just beeline to where the fish are reported; you cross the highest-probability water to get there. Decides pathing behaviour in every replan
evidence_needed: Replan logs: value collected en route vs arrival-time cost, across game types (open world vs level-based)

question: How short should the planning horizon get as a situation tightens, before the system asks the coach to grab the wheel
pole_low: stands down early, coach drives every tight spot personally
pole_high: keeps planning down to seconds, coach intervenes only on failure
why: The keyhole rule: first time through a tight passage with unknown wind and current, a responsible captain does not hand it to the autopilot. This question is the trust boundary of the whole product
evidence_needed: Coach takeover logs: which tight spots the coach chose to drive vs regretted delegating; near-miss reviews in debriefs

question: How large should a tile be: a single intention the coach can hold at once, or a chained routine that runs several intentions
pole_low: small tiles, coach assembles, overseer decides constantly
pole_high: large tiles, coach picks one and watches, overseer mostly idle
why: Granularity sets who thinks how often. Mindcraft's history is the evidence: parameterized commands won because they were the size of an intention, not an input and not a campaign
evidence_needed: Tile library statistics: reuse counts and failure rates by tile size; Mindcraft's command set as a worked example

question: When is a tile finished: when it works, or only when it passes the light-switch test and the coach forgets its mechanics entirely
pole_low: works is enough, graduation is a test pass
pole_high: invisible or unfinished, graduation requires the coach to use it for something else and never think about how
why: Casey's standard, 2026-10-14: the code has to be so good it goes invisible, like wiring behind a light switch. This question decides whether the library fills with tools or with appliances
evidence_needed: Graduation reviews in the workshop: tiles the coach had to ask about vs tiles never thought about again; explanation requests counted per tile

question: How strongly should a projected mechanic from creator transcripts be believed before it becomes a tile, given narration can exaggerate what the hands actually did
pole_low: only mechanics visible in outcomes count, narration is advertising
pole_high: narration counts as testimony, most stated mechanics become tiles pending disproof
why: The whole Codex-to-tiles pipeline stands on this: we project lower mechanics out of talk. Too strict and the library starves; too loose and it fills with theatre moves that never existed
evidence_needed: Projection audits: tiles built from transcripts, then tested in play — success rate by how the mechanic was evidenced (stated, shown in outcomes, or both)

question: While a tile runs, how patient should the overseer be with its slow start before judging it the wrong tile
pole_low: judges in seconds, wrong tiles die fast, right tiles sometimes die young
pole_high: judges on the tile's own timescale, slow starters get their full run
why: Every scripted behaviour has a wind-up (a troll pass needs the full pass). Impatient overseers thrash; patient ones ride disasters to the bottom. Pairs with the failure-dwell evidence from the Coach lane
evidence_needed: Tile abort logs vs outcomes had the tile finished; the format-change rule applied to aborts (was it the tile, or the situation)

question: How much of the question graph should ride into an authoring call when the LLM writes a new script
pole_low: only the questions about this exact situation, a narrow beam
pole_high: the whole relevant frontier: the situation, the game, the avatar's character, hundreds of shaded questions
why: Casey, 2026-10-14: the questioning projects into the call so the LLM starts from a vast array of how to make it better, not a blank prompt. Beam width trades focus against the accidents where distant questions turn out to be the point
evidence_needed: Authoring event logs: which priming questions the resulting script actually used, judged at verification and in later reuse

question: When the library holds several tiles that all fit, should the overseer pick the most proven, or rotate toward the least-tested that still clears the bar
pole_low: most proven always, sessions are reliable and a little samey
pole_high: rotate deliberately, sessions vary and the library learns from use
why: This is the exploration dial of the whole system, and it is where personality leaks in: two avatars with the same library play differently by this question alone
evidence_needed: Library health reports: usage concentration vs character distinctness in debriefs; whether rotation discoveries graduate or get pruned
